requirements.title: Access to variable routes by scope
requirements.rationale: A variable is configuration of its owner, so each scope decides who may read it and who may change it, and a caller without access must learn nothing.

criteria.condition: a PAT calls a variable list route without `vars:read` and without `vars:write`, or calls a variable create, update or delete route without `vars:write`
criteria.action: refuse the request before deciding scope access, and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`; the same answer for an existing and a nonexistent organization or workspace; a PAT with `vars:write` alone is served on the list routes; an API key and the admin token are served without any scope

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over {route: each of the 12 variable routes} x {credential: PAT without vars scopes, PAT vars:read, PAT vars:write, API key}: assert status 403 and error_type insufficient_scope exactly where the criterion says, on slug w and on slug nosuch alike; assert PAT vars:write gets 200 on GET /user/vars; assert the API key is never answered insufficient_scope

criteria.condition: the admin token calls any route under `/user/vars`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` and the message `user-scoped endpoints require a user credential`; nothing is stored, changed or deleted

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over POST /user/vars, GET /user/vars, PATCH /user/vars/A, DELETE /user/vars/A with the admin token: assert status 403; assert error_type == 'forbidden'; assert message == 'user-scoped endpoints require a user credential'; assert the variable table has no row of scope user

criteria.condition: a user calls a route under `/user/vars`
criteria.action: act on the variables whose scope is `user` and whose scope id is the caller's user id, and on no other user's
criteria.contract: an entry U created is listed for U and absent from the list of every other user

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go: as U POST /user/vars {entries:[{key:'A',value:'1'}]}; assert GET /user/vars as U lists A; assert GET /user/vars as M lists nothing; assert PATCH /user/vars/A as M is 404 not_found

criteria.condition: a route under `/orgs/:slug/vars` names an organization that does not exist, or an organization of which the calling user is not a member, or one that is blocked
criteria.action: answer as if the organization did not exist
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found`; the response body for an existing organization the caller is not a member of is byte-for-byte the body for a nonexistent slug; nothing is stored, changed or deleted

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over the four org routes and the callers {X on o, X on nosuch, U on nosuch, M on o after O is blocked}: assert status 404 and error_type not_found; assert body(X on o) == body(X on nosuch); assert no row was written

criteria.condition: a member of the organization, or the admin token, calls a route under `/orgs/:slug/vars`, naming the organization by its slug or its UUID
criteria.action: act on the variables whose scope is `org` and whose scope id is that organization's id
criteria.contract: a member creates, lists, updates and deletes the organization's variables; the admin token does the same without a membership, also on a blocked organization; the same entries are answered under the slug and under the UUID

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go: as M POST /orgs/o/vars creates A (201); as U GET /orgs/o/vars lists A; as U GET /orgs/<O.id>/vars lists the same items; as admin token PATCH /orgs/o/vars/A is 200 and DELETE is 204; block O, assert admin token GET /orgs/o/vars is 200

criteria.condition: a caller whose level on the workspace is `member` calls `POST /workspaces/:slug/vars`, `PATCH /workspaces/:slug/vars/:key` or `DELETE /workspaces/:slug/vars/:key`
criteria.action: refuse the write, whatever the body and whatever the workspace's status
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` and the message `org members have read-only access to this workspace`; the workspace's variables are unchanged; the same member is answered 200 on `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars`

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
W holds a variable A
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, as M on w, a table over POST (valid body, invalid body), PATCH A, DELETE A, each with W ready and W archived: assert status 403, error_type forbidden, message == 'org members have read-only access to this workspace'; assert rows unchanged; assert GET /workspaces/w/vars as M is 200

criteria.condition: a caller with no access level on the workspace calls any route under `/workspaces/:slug/vars`, or the slug names no workspace
criteria.action: answer as if the workspace did not exist
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` and the message `workspace not found`; the body for an existing workspace is byte-for-byte the body for a nonexistent slug; nothing is stored, changed or deleted

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
W holds a variable A
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over the five workspace routes (resolved included) with X on w and U on nosuch: assert status 404, error_type not_found, message == 'workspace not found'; assert body(X on w) == body(X on nosuch); assert rows unchanged

criteria.action: for any status of the workspace (`pending`, `cloning`, `ready`, `failed`, `archived`) and while the workspace is in an exclusive maintenance operation, serve the owner and the admin token on every route under `/workspaces/:slug/vars` as on a `ready` workspace
criteria.contract: no variable route answers `workspace_archived`, `workspace_not_ready` or `workspace_busy`

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over each workspace status and the maintenance marker set: as U POST a variable (201), GET list (200), PATCH (200), GET resolved (200), DELETE (204); as admin token GET list (200)

requirements.title: Creating variables
requirements.rationale: Configuration is usually set several keys at a time, and a half-applied set is worse than none.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access to the scope posts `{"entries":[{"key","value"}, …]}` to `POST /user/vars`, `POST /orgs/:slug/vars` or `POST /workspaces/:slug/vars` and every check passes
criteria.action: store every entry with the key casing given, treat a missing `value` as the empty string, and answer the created entries in request order
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with `{"items":[{key, value, created_at, updated_at}, …]}` and no other member per item; every item has the same `created_at`, equal to its `updated_at`, in RFC 3339 UTC with whole seconds; a key of 255 characters, a value of exactly 262,144 bytes and an empty value are accepted

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, for each of the three scopes: POST entries [{key:'Zed',value:'1'},{key:'alpha'},{key: 255 letters, value: 262144 bytes}] (the server body limit raised for the test); assert status 201; assert keys in request order with given casing; assert items[1].value == ''; assert every created_at == updated_at == the fixed clock's instant formatted with whole seconds; assert item members are exactly key, value, created_at, updated_at; assert GET lists the three

criteria.condition: the create body has no `entries`, an `entries` that is empty or not an array, an entry that is not an object, a key that is absent, not a string, empty, longer than 255 characters, starting with a digit or holding a character other than an ASCII letter, a digit or `_`, a value that is not a string or is longer than 262,144 bytes, or two keys equal ignoring case
criteria.action: refuse the whole request and store nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; for a fault of one entry the message contains that entry's key; the scope's variables are unchanged

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_validate_test.go and internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over the bodies {no entries, entries: [], entries: 'x', entries: [1], key absent, key: 7, key: '', key of 256 letters, key '1A', key 'A-B', key 'É', value: 5, value of 262145 bytes, value of 131073 two-byte characters, keys 'Foo' and 'FOO'} each beside one valid entry: assert status 400 and error_type invalid_request; assert the message contains the offending key where there is one; assert the list is still empty

criteria.condition: the number of variables already in the scope plus the number of entries in the request is more than 100
criteria.action: refuse the whole request, also when a key of the request already exists in the scope
criteria.contract: HTTP 429 with `error_type` `secret_limit_reached` and the message `maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded`; nothing is stored; a request that brings the scope to exactly 100 is answered 201; secrets of the same scope and variables of other scopes are not counted

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: seed 98 variables in W's scope and 100 in U's user scope; POST 2 new entries to /workspaces/w/vars -> 201 (count 100); POST 1 new entry -> 429, error_type secret_limit_reached, message == 'maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded'; POST 1 entry whose key already exists -> 429, not 409; assert count is still 100

criteria.condition: a key of the request is already present in the scope, compared ignoring case, and the scope is not full
criteria.action: refuse the whole request and store none of its entries
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict` and the message `key "<k>" already exists`, where `<k>` is the key as given in the request; the other entries of the request are not stored and the existing entry is unchanged

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: with variable 'Token' = 'old' in the scope, POST entries [{key:'NEW',value:'1'},{key:'TOKEN',value:'2'}]; assert status 409, error_type conflict, message == 'key "TOKEN" already exists'; assert the list holds only Token = old

criteria.action: for any create request with more than one fault, answer the fault that comes first in this order: `entries` not a non-empty array; an invalid key; an invalid value; two keys equal ignoring case; the scope's limit; a key already present
criteria.contract: the status and `error_type` are those of the first failing check

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over pairs of faults {invalid key + oversized value -> 400 naming the invalid key, oversized value + duplicate keys -> 400 naming the oversized entry's key, duplicate keys + full scope -> 400, full scope + existing key -> 429}: assert status, error_type and the key named

criteria.action: for any two concurrent create requests on one scope that carry the same key ignoring case, store the key once
criteria.contract: exactly one request is answered 201 and the other 409 `conflict`; the scope then holds one entry for the key, and none of the losing request's other entries

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_store_test.go: start 2 goroutines posting [{key:'k'},{key:'a1'}] and [{key:'K'},{key:'a2'}] to /workspaces/w/vars, repeated 20 times on fresh scopes; assert the statuses are {201, 409}; assert the scope holds exactly 2 entries, both from the winning request

criteria.condition: a create is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, caller, route and body within 24 hours of a successful create
criteria.action: create nothing and answer the original body
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the body of the original 201; the scope's entries are unchanged

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: POST /user/vars with Idempotency-Key k1 -> 201 body b; POST again with the same key and body -> 200 and body == b, not 409; assert the scope holds one entry

criteria.condition: no secret encryption key is configured
criteria.action: serve every variable route as when a key is configured
criteria.contract: no variable route answers 503 `secrets_unavailable`; create answers 201 and the value is read back unchanged

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, with the hub built without an encryption key: POST /user/vars -> 201; GET /user/vars -> 200 with the value; POST /workspaces/w/vars -> 201; POST /orgs/o/vars -> 201

requirements.title: Listing, updating and deleting variables
requirements.rationale: A value that can be set must be readable, changeable and removable by the name a person remembers, whatever casing they type.

criteria.condition: a caller with read access to the scope calls `GET /user/vars`, `GET /orgs/:slug/vars` or `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars`
criteria.action: answer that scope's own variables with their values, ordered by key ascending ignoring case, in pages
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{"items":[{key, value, created_at, updated_at}, …],"next_cursor":…}`; `items` is an array also when empty; `limit` defaults to 50 and `next_cursor` is null on the last page; a fork's list never holds its parent's variables

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
a fork F of a workspace that holds a variable P
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: seed keys 'b', 'A', 'c', 'B2' in W and 'P' in a parent of fork F; assert GET /workspaces/w/vars item keys == ['A','b','B2','c'] with values; assert GET with limit=2 then the cursor yields the same four once each and next_cursor null at the end; assert an empty scope answers items [] and next_cursor null; assert GET /workspaces/f/vars does not hold 'P'; seed 51 keys in U's scope and assert the first page holds 50

criteria.condition: a caller with write access to the scope sends `PATCH …/vars/:key` with `{"value": string}` and the key matches a variable of the scope ignoring case
criteria.action: replace the value, keep the stored key casing and `created_at`, and set `updated_at` to the current time
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the entry `{key, value, created_at, updated_at}`; `key` is the stored casing; the empty string is accepted as a value; a value of exactly 262,144 bytes is accepted

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, for each scope: create 'ApiUrl' = 'a' at t0; advance the clock to t1; PATCH …/vars/APIURL {value:'b'}; assert status 200, key == 'ApiUrl', value == 'b', created_at == t0, updated_at == t1; PATCH {value:''} -> 200 and value == ''; assert GET lists the new value

criteria.condition: the body of a `PATCH …/vars/:key` has no `value`, a `value` that is `null` or not a string, or a value longer than 262,144 bytes
criteria.action: refuse the request, whether or not the key exists, and leave the variable as it was
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the stored value and `updated_at` are unchanged

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over the bodies {{}, {value:null}, {value:3}, {value: 262145 bytes}} on an existing key and on a missing key: assert status 400 and error_type invalid_request; assert the entry is unchanged

criteria.condition: a `PATCH …/vars/:key` with a valid body or a `DELETE …/vars/:key` names a key that matches no variable of the scope ignoring case
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` and the message `key "<k>" not found`, where `<k>` is the key as given in the path; a key that exists only in another scope, or only as a secret of the same scope, is not a match

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over PATCH and DELETE on {a key never created, a key that exists in U's user scope addressed in W's scope, a key 'a-b' that no rule allows}: assert status 404, error_type not_found, message == 'key "<k>" not found'; assert no row changed

criteria.condition: a caller with write access to the scope sends `DELETE …/vars/:key` and the key matches a variable of the scope ignoring case
criteria.action: delete that variable
criteria.contract: HTTP 204 with an empty body; the key is absent from the scope's list afterwards and can be created again

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, for each scope: create 'Region'; DELETE …/vars/region; assert status 204 and len(body) == 0; assert GET does not list it; assert a second DELETE is 404; assert POST of 'REGION' is 201

criteria.condition: a request uses `PATCH` or `DELETE` on `/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved`, or `GET` on `/user/vars/:key`, `/orgs/:slug/vars/:key` or a `/workspaces/:slug/vars/:key` other than `resolved`
criteria.action: refuse the method without treating `resolved` as a key and without returning a single entry
criteria.contract: HTTP 405 with `error_type` `method_not_allowed` and an `Allow` header (`GET` for the resolved path; `PATCH, DELETE` for a key path); a variable stored under the key `resolved` is unchanged

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: create key 'resolved' in W; assert PATCH and DELETE /workspaces/w/vars/resolved are 405 method_not_allowed with Allow == 'GET' and the entry unchanged; assert GET /user/vars/A, GET /orgs/o/vars/A and GET /workspaces/w/vars/A are 405 with Allow naming PATCH and DELETE; assert PATCH /workspaces/w/vars/RESOLVED {value:'x'} is 200

requirements.title: Events for variable changes
requirements.rationale: Every change to configuration must be visible afterwards to the people who can see the scope, without the record ever holding a value.

criteria.condition: a create of variables succeeds
criteria.action: write one `parley.variable.create` event per created entry, in request order, in the same transaction as the entries
criteria.contract: each event has `resource_type` `variable`, `action` `create`, `resource_id` the stored key, the caller as actor, and `metadata` exactly `{"scope", "scope_id", "key"}` with scope `user`, `org` or `workspace` and scope id the user id, the organization id or the workspace slug; the event's `workspace` is the slug for the workspace scope and null for the other two

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
the real event component writing to the store
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_events_test.go, a table over the three scopes: POST two entries; read the event log; assert two parley.variable.create events in request order; assert resource_type, action, resource_id, actor, metadata == {scope, scope_id, key} and workspace == 'w' or null as the criterion says

criteria.condition: an update of a variable succeeds
criteria.action: write one `parley.variable.update` event with the fields of a create event and `action` `update`, in the same transaction as the update
criteria.contract: `resource_id` and `metadata.key` are the stored key casing, not the casing of the request path

the real event component writing to the store
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_events_test.go: create 'ApiUrl' in o; PATCH /orgs/o/vars/APIURL; assert exactly one new event, type parley.variable.update, action update, resource_id == 'ApiUrl', metadata.key == 'ApiUrl', metadata.scope == 'org', metadata.scope_id == O's id, workspace == null

criteria.condition: a delete of a variable succeeds
criteria.action: write one `parley.variable.delete` event with the fields of a create event and `action` `delete`, in the same transaction as the delete
criteria.contract: one event per deleted variable, with `resource_id` the key as it was stored

criteria.action: for any variable event, leave the variable's value out of every field of the event
criteria.contract: no member of a `parley.variable.*` event, its metadata included, equals or contains the value

criteria.condition: a create, update or delete of variables is refused with any error status, or a create is answered as an idempotent replay
criteria.action: write no variable event
criteria.contract: the event log holds the same events after the request as before it

the real event component writing to the store

criteria.condition: the event of a create, update or delete cannot be written
criteria.action: make no change to the variables and report a hub failure
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal` and a message that does not carry the cause; the scope's variables are as before the request

requirements.title: The resolution chain of a workspace
requirements.rationale: Variables and secrets must be looked up in one order that depends only on the workspace, so that every caller and every sandbox gets the same answer.

criteria.condition: the chain of a repository workspace is asked for
criteria.action: answer, highest priority first, the workspace's own `workspace` scope with origin `workspace`, the `org` scope of its organization with origin `org`, and the `user` scope of its owner with origin `user`
criteria.contract: an ordered list of steps, each with origin, scope and scope id; no step has origin `parent`

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/chain_test.go: chain(W) == [{workspace, workspace, 'w'}, {org, org, O.id}, {user, user, U.id}]

criteria.condition: the chain of a task fork is asked for
criteria.action: answer the fork's own `workspace` scope, then the parent's `workspace` scope with origin `parent`, then the `org` scope of the parent's organization, then the `user` scope of the fork's owner
criteria.contract: four steps in that order; the user step is the user who created the fork, not the parent's owner

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/chain_test.go: chain(F) == [{workspace, workspace, 'f'}, {parent, workspace, 'w'}, {org, org, O.id}, {user, user, M.id}]

criteria.condition: the workspace's owner is not a member of the workspace's organization, or that organization is blocked or no longer exists
criteria.action: leave the org step out of the chain and keep every other step
criteria.contract: the chain has no step with origin `org`; for a fork whose owner left the organization the parent step is still present

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/chain_test.go, a table over {M removed from O, O blocked, O deleted}: assert chain(F) has origins [workspace, parent, user]; with U removed from O assert chain(W) has origins [workspace, user]; re-add M and assert the org step is back at the next call

criteria.action: for any caller, the admin token included, build the chain from the workspace's owner and never from the caller
criteria.contract: the chain function takes no caller; the resolved route answers the same entries to the owner, to a member and to the admin token

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_vars_test.go: with a variable 'X' in U's user scope and a different 'X' in M's user scope, GET /workspaces/w/vars/resolved as U, as M and as the admin token; assert the three item lists are equal and X has U's value

criteria.condition: the chain is asked for a slug that names no workspace
criteria.action: answer a not-found error and no steps
criteria.contract: the function returns an error that callers can tell apart from a store failure as `workspace not found`; it never ends the process

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/chain_test.go: _, err = chain('nosuch'); assert errors.Is(err, the package's workspace-not-found error); with a store stub that fails, assert the error is not the not-found error

criteria.condition: a fork's parent record is missing, or the workspace's owner no longer exists as a user
criteria.action: leave that step out of the chain and answer the remaining steps
criteria.contract: no error; the chain has no `parent` step in the first case and no `user` step in the second

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/chain_test.go: delete user M (which also ends M's membership) and assert chain(F) origins == [workspace, parent] and err == nil; in a second store, remove W's record while F's stays and assert chain(F) origins == [workspace, org, user] and err == nil

requirements.title: Resolved variables of a workspace
requirements.rationale: An agent configures itself from the values its workspace or fork runs with, and needs to know where each one came from.

criteria.condition: a caller with read access to the workspace calls `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved`
criteria.action: merge the variables of the workspace's chain so that, for each key compared ignoring case, the entry of the highest-priority scope that has it is answered whole, and answer the merged entries ordered by key ascending ignoring case
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{"items":[{key, value, origin, created_at, updated_at}, …],"next_cursor":…}`; each key occurs once ignoring case; key casing, value and both timestamps are those of the winning entry; `origin` is `workspace`, `parent`, `org` or `user`; `limit` and `cursor` page the list as on every list

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_vars_test.go: seed user scope of U {A:'u', b:'u', D:'u'}, org O {a:'o', C:'o'}, W {B:'w'}; GET /workspaces/w/vars/resolved; assert items == [{a,'o',org}, {B,'w',workspace}, {C,'o',org}, {D,'u',user}] with each winner's timestamps; assert limit=2 and the cursor walk the same four once each; assert a workspace with an empty chain answers items [] and next_cursor null

criteria.condition: the workspace named is a task fork
criteria.action: include the parent workspace's variables with origin `parent`, below the fork's own and above the organization's
criteria.contract: a key only the parent has is answered with `origin` `parent`; a key the fork also has is answered with the fork's value and `origin` `workspace`; after the fork's entry is deleted the next read answers the parent's entry

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
a fork F (slug f) of W owned by M
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_vars_test.go: seed W {REGION:'eu', Mode:'p'}, O {MODE:'o', Org:'1'}, fork F {mode:'f'}; GET /workspaces/f/vars/resolved as M; assert REGION origin parent, mode value 'f' origin workspace, Org origin org; DELETE /workspaces/f/vars/mode as U (owner level on F); GET again as M; assert Mode value 'p' origin parent

criteria.action: for any caller, decide the resolved route by variable read access on the named workspace alone: the owner, the admin token and an org member are served, and a PAT needs `vars:read` or `vars:write`
criteria.contract: an org member who owns a fork is answered the parent's, the organization's and the fork owner's variables in the fork's resolved set without having write access to the parent; a member of the organization is answered the owner's user-scope variables of W in W's resolved set

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_vars_test.go: with 'OwnerOnly' in U's user scope, GET /workspaces/w/vars/resolved as M -> 200 and holds OwnerOnly origin user; as M with a PAT carrying only vars:write -> 200; as M with a PAT carrying neither -> 403 insufficient_scope; GET /user/vars as M does not hold OwnerOnly

criteria.condition: a fork's owner is no longer a member of the parent's organization
criteria.action: resolve the fork's variables without the org step and with the parent step, for the callers who can still reach the fork
criteria.contract: the parent's owner and the admin token are answered 200 with the fork's, the parent's and the fork owner's variables and none with `origin` `org`; the former member is answered 404 `not_found`

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
a fork F (slug f) of W owned by M
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_vars_test.go: seed W {P:'1'}, O {Q:'1'}, M's user scope {R:'1'}, fork F owned by M; remove M from O; GET /workspaces/f/vars/resolved as U and as admin token -> items keys == ['P','R'] with origins parent and user; as M -> 404 with message 'workspace not found'

criteria.condition: the store fails while the chain or a scope's variables are read
criteria.action: answer a hub failure and no partial list
criteria.contract: HTTP 500 with `error_type` `internal` and a message that does not carry the cause; no `items` member

setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_vars_test.go, with a variable reader stub that fails on the org step: GET /workspaces/w/vars/resolved; assert status 500, error_type internal, body has no items, message does not contain the stub's error text

requirements.title: Secrets by name along the chain
requirements.rationale: A sandbox gets its credentials and exposed secrets from the workspace it is attached to, and a fork of a read-only contributor must never receive what belongs to the parent.

criteria.condition: a component asks to resolve a list of secret names for a workspace slug
criteria.action: answer, for each distinct name in the order first asked, the value held by the first scope of the workspace's chain that has a secret of that name ignoring case, with that scope's origin
criteria.contract: per name: found with `value` and `origin` (`workspace`, `parent`, `org` or `user`), or missing; beside them the list of scopes searched, in chain order, each with origin, scope and scope id; an empty list of names answers no entries and no error; a secret whose value is the empty string is found

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go: store secrets user(U) {TOKEN:'u', Only_User:'x'}, org(O) {token:'o'}, workspace W {EMPTY:''}; r = resolve('w', ['TOKEN','only_user','EMPTY','NOPE','token']); assert r names in order TOKEN, only_user, EMPTY, NOPE; TOKEN value 'o' origin org; only_user value 'x' origin user; EMPTY found with value ''; NOPE missing; r.searched == [workspace w, org O, user U]; assert resolve('w', []) has no entries and err == nil

criteria.condition: the workspace is a task fork whose owner has write access to the parent workspace
criteria.action: search the parent's `workspace` scope as the second step for every name that is not a reserved name
criteria.contract: a secret only the parent has is found with `origin` `parent`; a secret the fork also has is found with the fork's value and `origin` `workspace`; the scopes searched hold the parent's scope

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go: store W {DEPLOY_KEY:'p', Both:'p'}, G {both:'g'}; r = resolve('g', ['DEPLOY_KEY','BOTH']); assert DEPLOY_KEY value 'p' origin parent; BOTH value 'g' origin workspace; r.searched origins == [workspace, parent, org, user]

criteria.condition: the workspace is a task fork whose owner has no write access to the parent workspace
criteria.action: skip the parent's `workspace` scope for every secret name, whoever asks, and never read a secret of the parent
criteria.contract: a secret only the parent has is missing; the scopes searched do not hold the parent's scope; the secret store receives no read for the parent's scope; the same fork still resolves the name from its own, the organization's and its owner's scope

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go, with a recording wrapper around the secret reader: store W {DEPLOY_KEY:'p'}, O {ORG_KEY:'o'}; r = resolve('f', ['DEPLOY_KEY','ORG_KEY']); assert DEPLOY_KEY missing; ORG_KEY value 'o' origin org; r.searched origins == [workspace, org, user]; assert the recorder saw no read with scope workspace and scope id 'w'

criteria.action: for any fork and any fork owner, skip the parent's `workspace` scope for the names `GIT_PAT`, `GIT_USERNAME`, `GIT_PASSWORD`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD` and `FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, compared ignoring case
criteria.contract: a reserved name stored only in the parent is missing for a fork of the parent's owner too, and the store receives no read of it in the parent's scope; the same name stored in the fork's own, the organization's or the owner's scope is found there

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go, with the recording wrapper, a table over the seven names in upper and lower case: store each in W; assert resolve('g', [name]) is missing and no read of that name hit scope id 'w'; then store GIT_PAT in U's user scope and assert resolve('g', ['git_pat']) is found with origin user

criteria.action: for any resolution, work out the chain and read the values at that call, keeping nothing from an earlier call
criteria.contract: after a secret is updated the next call answers the new value; after it is deleted from the winning scope the next call answers the next scope's value or missing; after the fork owner's write access to the parent ends the next call has no parent step, and after it returns the step is back

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go: resolve('g',['K']) == 'p' from parent; update K in W to 'p2' -> next call 'p2'; store K in G -> next call origin workspace; delete it -> origin parent again; change W's owner to another user through the record store -> next call K missing and no parent step; change it back -> found again

criteria.condition: the first scope of the chain that has a requested name holds a secret that cannot be read or decrypted
criteria.action: fail the whole resolution without consulting a lower scope for that name and without reporting the name as missing
criteria.contract: the function returns an error and no values; the error's text names the key and the scope and holds no secret value; the error can be told apart from `workspace not found`

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go: store K in W under key k1 and K = 'LOWER-MARKER' in U's user scope, plus OTHER = 'OTHER-MARKER' in W readable; reopen the secret store with a different key so W's K is undecryptable (or use a reader stub answering unreadable for W's K); r, err = resolve('w', ['OTHER','K']); assert err != nil and r has no values; assert err text contains 'K' and 'workspace'; assert it contains neither marker

criteria.condition: the slug names no workspace, or the store fails while the chain is built
criteria.action: answer an error and no values
criteria.contract: `workspace not found` for an unknown slug, any other error for a store failure; in both cases no value is returned and the process keeps running

setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W
the real secret store of internal/secret with a test encryption key
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/resolve_secrets_test.go: r, err = resolve('nosuch', ['K']); assert errors.Is(err, the package's workspace-not-found error) and r has no values; with a workspace record reader stub that fails, assert err != nil, err is not the not-found error and r has no values

requirements.title: Removal of variables with their owner
requirements.rationale: Configuration must not outlive what it configures, and a slug that is used again must not inherit the values of the workspace that had it before.

criteria.condition: the removal of a workspace or of a task fork runs this package's remover with its transaction and the slug
criteria.action: delete every variable whose scope is `workspace` and whose scope id is that slug, inside that transaction, and write no variable event
criteria.contract: after the transaction commits the slug has no variables; variables of other workspaces, of the parent, of users and of organizations are untouched; the remover returns no revoked token ids and the event log gains no `parley.variable.*` event

setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go: tx = store.Begin(); remove(tx, 'f'); tx.Commit(); assert count(workspace, 'f') == 0, count(workspace, 'w') == 3, count(user, U) == 2, count(org, O) == 2; assert no parley.variable event was written

criteria.condition: the transaction the remover ran in is rolled back, or the remover's delete fails
criteria.action: leave every variable of the slug in place, and return the failure to the caller of the remover
criteria.contract: after a rollback the slug's variables are listed as before; a failing delete returns a non-nil error, so that the removal's transaction is rolled back

setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go: tx = store.Begin(); remove(tx, 'w'); tx.Rollback(); assert count(workspace, 'w') == 3 and the values are unchanged; call remove with a transaction that is already closed and assert err != nil

criteria.condition: a workspace is created under a slug whose earlier workspace was removed
criteria.action: start the new workspace with no variables
criteria.contract: `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars` answers an empty `items`, and the resolved set holds no entry with `origin` `workspace`

setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
the variable routes mounted on a test hub
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go: run the remover for 'w' in a committed transaction together with deleting W's record; insert a new record with slug 'w'; assert GET /workspaces/w/vars items == []; assert no resolved item has origin workspace

criteria.condition: an admin deletes a user or an organization through DELETE /api/v1/users/:id or DELETE /api/v1/orgs/:id
criteria.action: delete the `user`-scope variables of that user or the `org`-scope variables of that organization in the transaction of the deletion, through the scope removers of internal/identity, and keep every other variable
criteria.contract: the delete answers 204 and the store holds no variable of the deleted user or organization; variables of other users, organizations and workspaces are unchanged; no `parley.variable.*` event is written

setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
a second user and a second organization with one variable each, which must survive
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go, with the real identity routes and this package's RemoveVarScope registered through RegisterUserRemover and RegisterOrgRemover: as admin DELETE /api/v1/users/<U.id> and DELETE /api/v1/orgs/<O.id>; assert both 204; assert count(user, U) == 0 and count(org, O) == 0; assert count(workspace, 'w') == 3 and the second user's and second organization's variables are still there; assert no parley.variable event

criteria.condition: the deletion of a user or an organization is refused, or its transaction is rolled back after this package's remover ran
criteria.action: leave every variable of that user or organization in place
criteria.contract: the variables of the scope are listed as before; a failing delete of variables returns a non-nil error to the deletion, which answers 500 `internal` and removes nothing

setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
the variable routes and the identity routes mounted on a test hub; M is a member of O
check.pseudocode: in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go: make U the only active admin and DELETE /api/v1/users/<U.id> -> 409; assert count(user, U) == 2; register after this package's remover a second org remover that returns an error; DELETE /api/v1/orgs/<O.id> -> 500 internal; assert count(org, O) == 2 and GET /orgs/o/vars as M still lists both

requirements.title: The parley vars commands
requirements.rationale: People and scripts set configuration from a shell, often for several scopes at once.

criteria.condition: `parley vars create` is run with entries given as `KEY=VALUE` arguments, several in one argument separated by commas, or as one bare `KEY` with `--from-stdin`
criteria.action: split each entry at its first `=`, read the value of a `--from-stdin` key from standard input without one trailing line ending, and send all entries in one `POST /<scope>/vars` body per scope
criteria.contract:
the request body is `{"entries":[{"key","value"}, …]}` in argument order; `A=b=c` sends value `b=c`; `A=` sends the empty value; with `--from-stdin` the input `line1
line2
` sends `line1
line2` and the input `v
` sends `v`

setup: the parley CLI run in-process through cli.Run with a hub URL and a credential set, against an httptest server that records each request and answers from a script
check.pseudocode:
in internal/cli/vars_test.go, a table over args {['A=1,B=x=y','C='] -> entries [A:'1', B:'x=y', C:''], ['K','--from-stdin'] with stdin 'line1
line2
' -> [K:'line1
line2'], stdin 'v
' -> [K:'v'], stdin 'a,b=c' -> [K:'a,b=c'], stdin '' -> [K:'']}: assert one POST to /api/v1/user/vars with exactly that body

criteria.condition: `parley vars create` is run with one or more of `--user`, `--org <slug>` and `--workspace <slug>`, or with none
criteria.action: send one create per scope given, in the order user, org, workspace whatever the order of the flags, to `/user/vars`, `/orgs/<slug>/vars` and `/workspaces/<slug>/vars`, and send only the user request when no flag is given
criteria.contract: stdout is one JSON document `{"results":[{"scope":"user"|"org"|"workspace","items":[…]}, …]}` in that order with each hub answer's `items`; exit status 0 when every scope succeeded

setup: the parley CLI run in-process through cli.Run with a hub URL and a credential set, against an httptest server that records each request and answers from a script
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/vars_test.go: run ['vars','create','A=1','--workspace','w','--user','--org','o']; assert the recorded requests are POST /api/v1/user/vars, /api/v1/orgs/o/vars, /api/v1/workspaces/w/vars in that order; assert stdout parses to results with scopes [user, org, workspace] and the scripted items; assert exit 0; run with no scope flag and assert one POST to /api/v1/user/vars and results == [{scope:'user', …}]

criteria.condition: the hub answers an error for one or more scopes of a `parley vars create`
criteria.action: still send the requests of the remaining scopes, print the scopes that succeeded, and report each failed scope once
criteria.contract: exit status 1; stdout is the `results` document holding only the scopes that succeeded (`{"results":[]}` when none did); stderr holds each failed scope's error envelope exactly once, as received

setup: the parley CLI run in-process through cli.Run with a hub URL and a credential set, against an httptest server that records each request and answers from a script
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/vars_test.go: script user -> 201, org -> 404 envelope, workspace -> 201; run create with the three flags; assert three requests were sent; assert stdout results scopes == [user, workspace]; assert stderr holds the 404 envelope once with error_type not_found; assert exit 1; script all three as errors and assert stdout == {results: []}, three envelopes on stderr, exit 1

criteria.condition: a `parley vars` command is given malformed arguments: an entry without `=` when `--from-stdin` is absent, an empty key, an empty entry between commas, `--from-stdin` with a number of arguments other than one or with an argument holding `=` or `,`, more than one entry for `update`, more than one scope flag on `list`, `update` or `delete`, a scope flag on `resolve`, or a wrong number of arguments
criteria.action: fail before sending any request
criteria.contract: exit status 2; nothing on stdout; stderr holds one error envelope with `code` 0 and `error_type` `usage_error`; the hub receives no request

setup: the parley CLI run in-process through cli.Run with a hub URL and a credential set, against an httptest server that records each request and answers from a script
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/vars_test.go, a table over args {create 'A', create '=v', create 'A=1,,B=2', create 'A=1' --from-stdin, create A B --from-stdin, create (no args), update 'A=1,B=2', update 'A=1' 'B=2', list --user --org o, update 'A=1' --org o --workspace w, delete A --user --workspace w, delete (no args), resolve w --user, resolve (no args)}: assert exit 2, stdout empty, stderr error_type usage_error with code 0, recorded request count == 0

criteria.condition: `parley vars list` is run with at most one scope flag
criteria.action: read `GET /<scope>/vars` with `limit=200`, follow `next_cursor` until it is null, and print the entries of all pages as one document
criteria.contract: stdout is `{"items":[…]}` with the items of every page in order, values included; exit status 0; a hub error on any page prints that envelope on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 1; the document has no `next_cursor` member

setup: the parley CLI run in-process through cli.Run with a hub URL and a credential set, against an httptest server that records each request and answers from a script

builds the workspace's chain, merges the scopes and answers log_level = debug with origin workspace
deletes /workspaces/:slug/vars/LOG_LEVEL and reads the resolved set again
deletes the workspace's entry, writes parley.variable.delete and answers LOG_LEVEL = info with origin org

execution_paths.title: An org member's fork runs with the parent's variables and without its secrets

resolves the secret DEPLOY_KEY for the member's fork: the fork's owner has no write access to the parent, so the parent's scope is skipped and the name is missing
resolves the same name for a fork the developer owns and finds it with origin parent
